clue.text: Country: one embracing American culture, initially

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the word for one holds the other letters within it

parts.note: mono- is the prefix meaning one, as in monologue

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style entry: a country described as one that welcomes American culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes A and C from 'American culture'; MONO 'embracing' them gives MON-AC-O.
explanation.definitionFit: Monaco is a tiny sovereign principality on the Riviera, so it is a country.

clue.text: Plant one male on top of another

indicators.note: in a down answer, on top of puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a man is one male
another male: a drake is a male duck

explanation.surface: A plant positioned with one man stacked on another.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandrake is a plant with a forked root, famed in folklore for shrieking when pulled up.

clue.text: A tad snowy, though no time to shiver in the current climate

indicators.note: to shiver is to shake, so the remaining letters are shaken into a new order
no means without, so this letter is dropped from the fodder

explanation.surface: A weather note: a little snowy, yet not cold enough to make you shiver these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no time' removes T from ATADSNOWY, and 'to shiver' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means at the present time, as things stand now.

definitions.meaning: a doctor's ... is a patient being treated

explanation.definitionFit: Case means both a person under medical care and a suit brought in court.

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or bad, so the letters of races are disordered

parts.note: to have got something is to have understood it

explanation.surface: Someone checks that a listener has grasped that the races are off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'races off' reads like a cancelled meeting, but 'off' is the anagram signal working on races.
explanation.definitionFit: An escargot is a snail, the proverbial creature that crawls along at a sluggish pace.

clue.text: No more fixtures need to be rearranged

indicators.note: rearranged plainly means the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A fixture list must be reorganised because games are cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Six feet under is an idiom for dead and buried, so no longer living.

indicators.note: unseen at the start means the opening letter goes missing

parts.note: a fairy is a supernatural spirit

explanation.surface: A faint ghost first goes unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy room is light and spacious, full of air and brightness.

clue.text: Lady exposed, as shout of encouragement heard at Covent Garden?

parts.note: a cheer urging someone on, as fans yell at a runner
a diva, a leading soprano, is someone heard at the Royal Opera House

explanation.surface: An opera singer is exposed as the crowd cheers her on at Covent Garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' tempts a homophone, but the phrase simply names a singer at London's Royal Opera House in Covent Garden: GO + DIVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Godiva legendarily rode naked through Coventry, so she is the lady exposed.

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: to seek to do something is to try
a tip is an end

explanation.surface: Someone tries to keep a gratuity for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' could be a gratuity or advice; here it is an end.
explanation.definitionFit: In, as in fashionable, is a synonym of trendy: what is in is in vogue.

clue.text: Most fresh, figure nursing stitch on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means the whole assembled string is read from right to left
nursing means holding close, so the number word holds the stitching word inside it

parts.note: ten is a figure, that is a number
to stitch is to sew

explanation.surface: A figure, perhaps a nurse, tends a stitch while travelling home, at her freshest.
explanation.walkthrough: TEN 'nursing' SEW gives T-SEW-EN, and 'on the way back' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Newest is the superlative of new, and something new is fresh, so most fresh is newest.

clue.text: Ambitious student's target unknown in old game

indicators.note: in places the unknown letter inside the other letters

parts.note: bridge is a card game
in algebra an unknown quantity is written x

explanation.surface: An ambitious student aims for some mysterious old game.
explanation.walkthrough: OXBRIDGE is the joint name for the universities of Oxford and Cambridge, England's most prestigious.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting into Oxford or Cambridge is the classic goal of a high-achieving British school pupil.

parts.note: bouncy means lively and exuberant
a castle is a chess man, another name for the rook

explanation.surface: A lively fellow who amuses children, perhaps a party clown.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouncy castle is an inflatable play structure that keeps children amused at parties.

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An advert offering free energy for your journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to travel on a horse, bike or vehicle.

parts.note: love means nothing, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Romeo is left with nothing, which is just as it should be.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Romeo is the archetypal lover, and a romeo is any ardent wooer.

parts.note: vid is short for video, a taped recording

explanation.surface: A sex tape described as passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: An avid fan is a keen, eager one, so passionate is a close synonym.

clue.text: House where every one of four brought up

indicators.note: in a down answer, brought up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: all means every one
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A house where all four children were raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large house, typically a country or holiday residence.

clue.text: /Skill drawing up line on this organ

indicators.note: drawing up in a down answer means pulling the word upwards, so it reads in reverse

parts.note: an arc is a curved line
this organ is the newspaper the puzzle appears in, the Financial Times or FT

explanation.surface: Skill in drafting a line for this publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' is a newspaper here, the FT itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft is a trade requiring skill, and craft also means skill itself.

clue.text: As Greek unity crumbling, score mark?

indicators.note: crumbling means breaking apart, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: As Greek political unity collapses, someone wonders whether to mark the score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' is musical notation, not a tally.
explanation.definitionFit: A key signature is the set of sharps or flats marked at the start of a stave in written music.

definitions.meaning: turning into, as in growing old

explanation.definitionFit: Becoming is an adjective for suitable attire and a participle for gradually turning into something.

clue.text: Old vow in due course for heathen

parts.note: "I do" is the time-honoured vow said at a wedding
in due course means later

explanation.surface: An ancient pledge to be fulfilled at some point by a pagan.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, so to a believer they are a heathen.

parts.note: a team playing another is up against it
a field is a sphere of activity or study

explanation.surface: Someone parks their car up against a sphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Park' looks like a verb; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A playing field is an open grassy space for games, much like a public park.

clue.text: Old instrument group used to bandage leg

indicators.note: a bandage wraps around, so the group word wraps the leg word

parts.note: a set is a group
pin is slang for leg

explanation.surface: A team uses an antique instrument to strap up a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord, a keyboard instrument of the past.

clue.text: Heading off, soldiers given tip take the King's shilling

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: men is a common word for soldiers
to tip over or lean is to list, as a ship does

explanation.surface: Soldiers set off, given a tip-off about joining up.
explanation.walkthrough: To take the King's shilling is an old British idiom for joining the army, from the coin once given to recruits.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlisting is signing up for military service, which the idiom describes.

clue.text: Location of water fountain's back inside school

indicators.note: inside puts the last letter within the school word

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A fountain stands behind a school building, beside some water.
explanation.definitionFit: A pond is a small body of still water.

indicators.note: shocking means scandalous, a hint that the letters of rates are thrown about

explanation.surface: An outraged cry about scandalous prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' does double duty in spirit: the anagram signal, and the weapon's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is a stun gun that delivers an electric shock to disable someone.

indicators.note: something under discussion is being talked about, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: a foul is an infringement in football

explanation.surface: A football wide player's foul is debated by pundits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A fowl is a bird, and birds are creatures with wings.

indicators.note: hosted by means held within, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A party thrown by a wife turns out boring.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor festival or gala, often with stalls and games.

indicators.note: in a down answer, popping up means the word rises, read in reverse

parts.note: nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: A fish pokes its head up from the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish.

indicators.note: in places the pieces before it inside the document word

parts.note: a note is a short written document
to set something is to put it down

explanation.surface: A cook puts a fillet into a recipe document.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a small round boneless cut of meat, such as lamb, so a kind of fillet.

indicators.note: confined to means shut inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a nick is a small cut
bis is a musical direction meaning twice or again

explanation.surface: A painter is locked up in a police station again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' is British slang for a police station or prison, misleading here; it is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cubist is an artist of the movement led by Picasso and Braque.

clue.text: Number inspired by inspirational talker unable to break free

indicators.note: inspired literally means breathed in, so the talker takes the number inside

parts.note: TED talks are famous inspirational lectures
ether is a number, an anaesthetic that numbs

explanation.surface: A figure drawn in by a motivational speaker finds themselves trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is something that makes numb, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A tethered animal is tied by a rope and so cannot get loose.

definitions.meaning: the ... has a striped black and white face

explanation.surface: A dog chases a monochrome creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Badger means pester as a verb and names a striped burrowing mammal as a noun.
